body.facts:
https://github.com/NickMele/armada/issues/570

Reclaiming a finished Job's disk from the board deletes its record

Clearing the board is the only bulk act on it, and it deletes every finished Job's whole record — the log, the checks, the judgments and the workflow results go along with the worktree the person was trying to reclaim. The owner asked for exactly the opposite on #560, that PR merged, and on 9 Sep 2026 he found the button unchanged: it fixed `armada clean` and never touched the Board. Getting disk back still costs the history of what was built on it.

## What happened

`#560` gave `armada clean` `Store::retain_job`, so a CLI sweep now keeps the record. The Board does not go through `armada clean`. `Clearing.clearTerminal` (`apps/desktop/src/main/clearing.ts:57`) loops `forget_job` per id — real deletion — and `ClearTerminalControl`'s dialog says so in as many words: *"removed from the board along with its whole record. There is no undo, and a cleared job cannot be opened again."*

The act the button should be sending already exists on the wire. `reclaim_worktree` takes one terminal Job's worktree and branch and leaves the row exactly where it is, and Bridge already sends it one Job at a time from the job detail (`commands.ts`'s `act`). Nothing bulk reaches it.

Two gaps sit behind the swap:

- **`Fleet::reclaim_worktree` never calls `Store::retain_job`.** Only `armada clean` does, at `crates/armada/src/clean.rs:540`. The live path leaves `job_drone_process` holding a pid whose worktree it just deleted — the stale row `retain_job` exists to clear.
- **A reclaim marks nothing.** No column on `jobs` records that a Job's disk was given back, so a board after a clear looks identical to one before it, and the button reads as having done nothing.

**Ports need no work.** `port-range-base`, `port-range-ceiling` and `port-block-granule` in `crates/config/settings.toml` are design; no code claims, holds or hands out a port span. There is nothing to release. **Processes need nothing beyond the pid row** either — a terminal Job holds no live Drone, and `kill_job` is what ends one still in flight.

## In

| Seam | Change |
|---|---|
| `crates/store/src/schema.rs`, `retain.rs` | A `reclaimed_at` column on `jobs`, stamped by `retain_job`. This is the marker everything below reads; without it nothing can tell a cleared Job from a finished one. |
| `crates/fleet/src/reclaiming.rs` | `reclaim_worktree` calls `retain_job` after `adapters::reclaim` succeeds. |
| `crates/ipc`, `packages/protocol` | `reclaimed_at` on the Job read shape, regenerated into TypeScript. Additive, so `protocol-version.toml` moves `minor`, not `major`. |
| `apps/desktop/src/main/clearing.ts` | `clearTerminal` loops `reclaim_worktree` instead of `forget_job`. A second bulk act sends `forget_job`, keeping the two sets `Clearing` already holds apart. |
| `packages/screens/src/Jobs.tsx`, `packages/components/src/compositions/BoardControls` | A `Cleared` tab carrying reclaimed Jobs, and a `Finished` tab that no longer does. |
| `packages/shell/src/ClearTerminal.tsx`, the job detail acts | Rewrite the dialog, which currently promises the deletion this issue removes. Add a per-Job `Delete record` act and the bulk one beside `Clear`, each with its own destructive confirm. |

## Watch for

- **Do not fold the reclaim into `forget_job`.** `crates/ipc/operations.toml` argues the split on both rows — one call with two unrelated things to fail at is worse than two calls — and a caller wanting both sends both.
- **Do not add a force.** `reclaim_worktree` runs `UnmergedWork::Keep` and there is deliberately no equivalent of `armada clean --force` on this seam: a live Fleet must not be the thing that destroys work nobody has taken. A branch left standing is part of a successful answer, and a bulk clear does not change that. The bulk outcome has to carry which branches survived, or the sentence a person reads will be wrong for some of them.
- **Do not derive `cleared` from the worktree being absent.** A directory that is gone for some other reason is not a record of an act, and `armada clean`'s own module makes the same argument about deriving from a record rather than matching a pattern.
- **Do not remove the forget.** Both the per-Job delete and a bulk one stay in Bridge; the owner decided that on 9 Sep 2026. It is the one act on this seam that cannot be undone, so it keeps its own confirm and does not share `Clear`'s.
- **A reclaim that fails does not stop the sweep.** `clearTerminal` already collects per-id failures, and the shape it answers with (`ClearOutcome`) survives the swap.

## Definition of done

- Clearing the finished jobs from the board gives the worktrees and branches back, and every one of those jobs still opens with its log, its checks and its workflow results.
- Cleared jobs are under their own tab, and are not in the finished tab.
- After a clear from the board, no `job_drone_process` row survives for a job whose worktree was removed — a store test asserts it through `Fleet::reclaim_worktree`, not through `armada clean`.
- Deleting a record is still possible, on one job and in bulk, and says that it cannot be undone.
- A branch the base cannot reach survives a bulk clear, and the person is told which ones did.

## How this was found

The owner asked for it on #560: *"when cleaning up jobs, what we really want to do is reclaim the resources that were occupied by the jobs … but we want to keep a record of the work."* That Job read the request as `armada clean`'s and shipped `Store::retain_job`, which is right and is half of it. He pressed the button on 9 Sep 2026 and the jobs were gone.

Now compiling the full findings report.

## Findings, by claim

**1. `apps/desktop/src/main/clearing.ts` — `Clearing.clearTerminal`**
Discrepancy on the line number, confirmed on behavior. The file is only 122 lines total; `clearTerminal` is at `apps/desktop/src/main/clearing.ts:59-67`, not line 57 (close, off by ~2 — check whether the issue was written against a slightly different revision).

- `clearTerminal(jobIds)` (lines 59-67) does exactly what the issue assumes: it loops and calls `this.forget(jobId)` per id (line 62), collecting `cleared`/`failed`, and returns `ClearOutcome`.
- `ClearOutcome` shape (imported from `@armada/protocol`, used at line 65): `{ cleared: string[]; failed: { jobId: string; outcome: Outcome }[] }`.
- The private `forget(jobId)` (lines 105-121) is a **forget-only** path: it POSTs `forget_job` (line 114) and, on success, calls `board.forget(jobId)` — real deletion of the row.
- There is **also** a public `reclaim(jobId)` method (lines 74-96) already in this file, which POSTs `reclaim_worktree` and returns a receipt (`Outcome` with `reclaimed: WorktreeReclaimed`), leaving the Job row untouched. This is the single-job path already wired into the job detail's "act" menu, but `clearTerminal` (the bulk board button) does **not** call it — it only ever calls `forget`. This is the crux of the issue: the bulk clear-board path has no reclaim step, and adding it is squarely "extend this file," not "invent new plumbing" — `reclaim` and `ClearOutcome`-shaped bulk aggregation both already exist as patterns/pieces here.
- No other bulk method exists in the file. There is no bulk `reclaim_worktree` route on the wire either (the file's own doc comment on `clearTerminal` says so: "there is no bulk route on the wire").

**2. Bridge `commands.ts` — single-job `reclaim_worktree` act**
Confirmed. In `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/commands.ts`'s `act()` function (~line 173), `reclaim_worktree` dispatches to `window.armada.reclaimWorktree(jobId)`. Full chain:
- Preload: `apps/desktop/src/preload/index.ts:86-87` — `reclaimWorktree: (jobId: string): Promise<Outcome> => ipcRenderer.invoke(CHANNELS.reclaimWorktree, jobId)`.
- Bridge type: `apps/desktop/src/shared/bridge.ts:342` — `reclaimWorktree: (jobId: string) => Promise<Outcome>`.
- Main handler: `apps/desktop/src/main/index.ts:290-291` and `apps/desktop/src/main/command.ts:351` → `Clearing.reclaim(jobId)` → `ask(port, "POST", route(jobId, "reclaim_worktree"))` (`apps/desktop/src/main/clearing.ts:89`).

Signature is **just a job id** — no explicit worktree path or branch name is passed anywhere in this chain. Worktree/branch are derived server-side from the job id via `WorktreeSpec::for_job` (see claim 3). So any plan proposing to pass worktree+branch through IPC would be adding parameters that don't exist today; the existing contract is id-only.

**3. Rust: `Fleet::reclaim_worktree` and `Store::retain_job`**
Important discrepancy found here — **`Fleet::reclaim_worktree` does NOT call `Store::retain_job` today.**

- `crates/fleet/src/reclaiming.rs:59-85`: `Fleet::reclaim_worktree(&self, job_id: &JobId) -> Result<Reclaimed, Adrift>` loads the job, checks it's terminal, builds a `WorktreeSpec::for_job(...)`, and calls `adapters::reclaim(&spec, self.manifest().base(), UnmergedWork::Keep)`. That's it — no store write of any kind. The module doc explicitly says "**The record is untouched**" and doesn't mention touching `job_drone_process`.
- `adapters::reclaim` is in `crates/adapters/src/reclaim.rs:293` — pure git/filesystem work (remove worktree, then delete branch per `UnmergedWork`), no database interaction at all; it doesn't know the Store exists.
- `Store::retain_job` **does** exist, at `crates/store/src/retain.rs:44-63`. It: checks whether the job row exists (`existed`), deletes from `job_drone_process WHERE job_id = ?1` (`drone_process` flag = whether a row was actually deleted), and returns `Retained { existed, drone_process }`. It touches no `reclaimed_at`-style column — there isn't one (see claim 5).
- The **only caller** of `Store::retain_job` in non-test code is `crates/armada/src/clean.rs:540` (the CLI sweep), not the live-Fleet `reclaim_worktree` operation. So today there are two disconnected "reclaim" implementations: the CLI's `armada clean` sweep (worktree/branch reclaim + `retain_job` for the DB row), and Fleet's live `reclaim_worktree` HTTP operation (worktree/branch reclaim only, no DB touch). If the issue's premise is "reclaim_worktree already calls retain_job," that's wrong — this is presumably exactly the gap the fix needs to close (make the live path also clear `job_drone_process`, the way the CLI sweep does).

**4. `crates/armada/src/clean.rs` around line 540**
Confirmed. Lines 538-542:
```
let outcome = match keep {
    Keep::Record => store.retain_job(job_id).map(RecordOutcome::Retained),
    Keep::Nothing => store.forget_job(job_id).map(RecordOutcome::Forgotten),
};
```
`Keep` is a two-variant enum at `crates/armada/src/clean.rs:443-449`: `Record` ("Keep the record. Only `job_drone_process` is cleared.") vs `Nothing` ("the row goes through `Store::forget_job`, as every id did before this feature"). The module doc (top of file, lines 1-23) states the semantics directly: "**Reclaiming a Job's disk is not forgetting the Job.** A folded Job keeps its row, its log and its results: `Store::retain_job` clears only what this act made stale, the live Drone process. `forget_job` is still real [deletion]." This is the clean statement of "retain" vs "forget"/"cleared" semantics the issue brief needs: retain = disk reclaimed, record (job row, events, checks, judgments, evidence) kept; forget = full row deletion including that history.

**5. `crates/store/src/schema.rs` — `jobs` table columns**
Confirmed no reclaimed/cleared marker column exists. `jobs` table, `crates/store/src/schema.rs:127-154`:
```
job_id, status, workflow_id, owner_manifest_id, origin, urgency, atomic, model,
acceptance_criteria, current_step_id, assigned_drone, dependencies,
dispatched_by_job_id, dispatched_by_step_id, redispatched_from, subject_kind,
subject_ref, facts, scope_revisions, write_targets_known, created_at
```
No `reclaimed_at`, no `cleared_at`, no `disk_reclaimed` flag or anything similar anywhere in `schema.rs` (grepped for `reclaimed_at`/`cleared_at` across the file — zero hits). So today, whether a terminal job's worktree has already been reclaimed is **not recorded on the job row at all** — it's only observable indirectly via `job_drone_process` having been cleared, or by disk state itself. If the planned "Cleared" tab (claim 8) needs to distinguish "terminal and reclaimed" from "terminal and not yet reclaimed," there is currently no column to read that from; this would need either a new column/event or a client-side signal (e.g., watching the `WorktreeReclaimed` receipt).

**6. `job_drone_process` table — lifecycle and the "stale row" claim**
Partially confirmed, with an important nuance.

- Table: `crates/store/src/process.rs:54-62` — `job_drone_process(job_id PK, step_id, drone_id, pid, started_at, spawned_at)`, one row per job while its Drone process is live.
- Created by `Store::record_drone_process` (`process.rs:96`) when a Drone spawns.
- Cleared two ways: (a) normally, by `Store::forget_drone_process` (`process.rs:145-154`), called from `Fleet::drone_left` (`crates/fleet/src/drone_moves.rs:151-165`) — this fires whenever Fleet records that a Drone's process has exited, which is the ordinary path a job takes on its way to terminal; and (b) via `Store::retain_job`'s own `DELETE FROM job_drone_process` (`retain.rs:55`), used by the CLI sweep.
- The doc comment on `Retained::drone_process` (`retain.rs:29-32`) states the field is "`false` on a Job whose Drone had already left, **which is the ordinary shape by the time a sweep reaches a terminal Job**." That is, in the common case, `job_drone_process` is *already* cleared by `drone_left` before a job even goes terminal — `retain_job`'s deletion there is mostly a no-op safety net, not the primary clearer.
- So the issue's claim that live `reclaim_worktree` "leaves a stale `job_drone_process` row" is only true in the **non-ordinary** case: a job that reached a terminal status without `drone_left` having run and cleared the row first (e.g., a killed job, or a Fleet restart/crash edge case where the process record wasn't cleaned up before the status moved). It is not true that every reclaimed job has a stale row — but since `Fleet::reclaim_worktree` calls neither `retain_job` nor `forget_drone_process` (confirmed under claim 3), whatever row does exist at reclaim time is left untouched by the live path today. The act the button should be sending already exists on the wire. `reclaim_worktree` takes one terminal Job's worktree and branch and leaves the row exactly where it is, and Bridge already sends it one Job at a time from the job detail (`commands.ts`'s `act`). Nothing bulk reaches it.

- **`Fleet::reclaim_worktree` never calls `Store::retain_job`.** Only `armada clean` does, at `crates/armada/src/clean.rs:540`. The live path leaves `job_drone_process` holding a pid whose worktree it just deleted — the stale row `retain_job` exists to clear.
- **A reclaim marks nothing.** No column on `jobs` records that a Job's disk was given back, so a board after a clear looks identical to one before it, and the button reads as having done nothing.

**Ports need no work.** `port-range-base`, `port-range-ceiling` and `port-block-granule` in `crates/config/settings.toml` are design; no code claims, holds or hands out a port span. Board's clear button should reclaim worktrees, not delete records

https://github.com/NickMele/armada/issues/570

Reclaiming a finished Job's disk from the board deletes its record

Clearing the board is the only bulk act on it, and it deletes every finished Job's whole record — the log, the checks, the judgments and the workflow results go along with the worktree the person was trying to reclaim. The owner asked for exactly the opposite on #560, that PR merged, and on 9 Sep 2026 he found the button unchanged: it fixed `armada clean` and never touched the Board. Getting disk back still costs the history of what was built on it.

## What happened

`#560` gave `armada clean` `Store::retain_job`, so a CLI sweep now keeps the record. The Board does not go through `armada clean`. `Clearing.clearTerminal` (`apps/desktop/src/main/clearing.ts:57`) loops `forget_job` per id — real deletion — and `ClearTerminalControl`'s dialog says so in as many words: *"removed from the board along with its whole record. There is no undo, and a cleared job cannot be opened again."*

The act the button should be sending already exists on the wire. `reclaim_worktree` takes one terminal Job's worktree and branch and leaves the row exactly where it is, and Bridge already sends it one Job at a time from the job detail (`commands.ts`'s `act`). Nothing bulk reaches it.

Two gaps sit behind the swap:

- **`Fleet::reclaim_worktree` never calls `Store::retain_job`.** Only `armada clean` does, at `crates/armada/src/clean.rs:540`. The live path leaves `job_drone_process` holding a pid whose worktree it just deleted — the stale row `retain_job` exists to clear.
- **A reclaim marks nothing.** No column on `jobs` records that a Job's disk was given back, so a board after a clear looks identical to one before it, and the button reads as having done nothing.

**Ports need no work.** `port-range-base`, `port-range-ceiling` and `port-block-granule` in `crates/config/settings.toml` are design; no code claims, holds or hands out a port span. There is nothing to release. **Processes need nothing beyond the pid row** either — a terminal Job holds no live Drone, and `kill_job` is what ends one still in flight.

## In

| Seam | Change |
|---|---|
| `crates/store/src/schema.rs`, `retain.rs` | A `reclaimed_at` column on `jobs`, stamped by `retain_job`. This is the marker everything below reads; without it nothing can tell a cleared Job from a finished one. |
| `crates/fleet/src/reclaiming.rs` | `reclaim_worktree` calls `retain_job` after `adapters::reclaim` succeeds. |
| `crates/ipc`, `packages/protocol` | `reclaimed_at` on the Job read shape, regenerated into TypeScript. Additive, so `protocol-version.toml` moves `minor`, not `major`. |
| `apps/desktop/src/main/clearing.ts` | `clearTerminal` loops `reclaim_worktree` instead of `forget_job`. A second bulk act sends `forget_job`, keeping the two sets `Clearing` already holds apart. |
| `packages/screens/src/Jobs.tsx`, `packages/components/src/compositions/BoardControls` | A `Cleared` tab carrying reclaimed Jobs, and a `Finished` tab that no longer does. |
| `packages/shell/src/ClearTerminal.tsx`, the job detail acts | Rewrite the dialog, which currently promises the deletion this issue removes. Add a per-Job `Delete record` act and the bulk one beside `Clear`, each with its own destructive confirm. |

## Watch for

- **Do not fold the reclaim into `forget_job`.** `crates/ipc/operations.toml` argues the split on both rows — one call with two unrelated things to fail at is worse than two calls — and a caller wanting both sends both.
- **Do not add a force.** `reclaim_worktree` runs `UnmergedWork::Keep` and there is deliberately no equivalent of `armada clean --force` on this seam: a live Fleet must not be the thing that destroys work nobody has taken. A branch left standing is part of a successful answer, and a bulk clear does not change that. The bulk outcome has to carry which branches survived, or the sentence a person reads will be wrong for some of them.
- **Do not derive `cleared` from the worktree being absent.** A directory that is gone for some other reason is not a record of an act, and `armada clean`'s own module makes the same argument about deriving from a record rather than matching a pattern.
- **Do not remove the forget.** Both the per-Job delete and a bulk one stay in Bridge; the owner decided that on 9 Sep 2026. It is the one act on this seam that cannot be undone, so it keeps its own confirm and does not share `Clear`'s.
- **A reclaim that fails does not stop the sweep.** `clearTerminal` already collects per-id failures, and the shape it answers with (`ClearOutcome`) survives the swap.

## Definition of done

- Clearing the finished jobs from the board gives the worktrees and branches back, and every one of those jobs still opens with its log, its checks and its workflow results.
- Cleared jobs are under their own tab, and are not in the finished tab.
- After a clear from the board, no `job_drone_process` row survives for a job whose worktree was removed — a store test asserts it through `Fleet::reclaim_worktree`, not through `armada clean`.
- Deleting a record is still possible, on one job and in bulk, and says that it cannot be undone.
- A branch the base cannot reach survives a bulk clear, and the person is told which ones did.
